title: US National Guard Recruitment 2026: Requirements & Benefits
metaDescription: US National Guard recruitment 2026: ages 17 to 42, part-time service alongside a civilian career, ASVAB screening, education benefits and an 8-year obligation.
headline: Joining the US National Guard in 2026: Requirements and Benefits

sections.title: Who can join
sections.content:
The Army National Guard accepts non-prior-service applicants aged 17 to 42, with 17-year-olds needing parental or guardian consent. Applicants must be US citizens or qualifying permanent residents for enlisted service, while commissioning generally requires US citizenship. A high school diploma or qualifying equivalent is required, and applicants must pass the ASVAB with a minimum AFQT score of 31.

Applicants must also meet Department of Defense medical standards, body-composition standards, and moral and administrative screening. Some conditions that require extra review can be waived, so a condition is not always an automatic disqualification. Prior-service applicants and specialty programs, such as OCS or Special Forces, may use different age rules.

sections.title: The part-time service model
sections.content:
Unlike active-duty soldiers, most National Guard members serve part-time, typically training one weekend a month plus two weeks a year, while balancing civilian careers or higher education. This flexibility makes the Guard attractive to students, professionals, and people seeking personal and professional growth alongside military service.

Guard soldiers can be called upon to respond to natural disasters, assist during emergencies, support homeland security operations, participate in humanitarian missions, and deploy overseas for military operations. When mobilized for state or federal missions, service becomes full-time, with full-time pay and benefits.

sections.title: Training path
sections.content:
The process starts with contacting a local Army or Air National Guard recruiter, taking the ASVAB, passing a medical exam at a Military Entrance Processing Station, and signing an enlistment contract. Most contracts carry an eight-year service obligation, typically split between active drilling status and the Individual Ready Reserve.

After signing, recruits attend Basic Combat Training, followed by job-specific Advanced Individual Training. Some applicants who exceed body-fat standards at MEPS may be routed through a preparatory physical training course first. Age eligibility is measured against the ship date for basic training, not the signing date.

sections.title: Benefits of serving
sections.content:
Members earn military pay and allowances, education benefits such as the GI Bill and tuition assistance, access to TRICARE Reserve Select health coverage, VA home loan eligibility, and retirement points toward a military pension. Many states also offer additional tuition waivers at public colleges for Guard members in good standing.

Service also builds leadership, teamwork, and technical skills that transfer to civilian careers, plus access to on-base commissary and exchange privileges. Guard members gain the chance to travel for training and missions, serve their own communities during crises, and build a second career alongside their civilian profession.

faqs.q: How old do you have to be to join the National Guard?
faqs.a: You must be between 17 and 42 years old to enlist in the Army National Guard as a non-prior-service applicant, with 17-year-olds needing parental consent. Prior-service applicants can sometimes exceed that limit because creditable service years are subtracted from their age. Each state's Guard unit may apply slightly different rules for specialty programs.

faqs.q: Is National Guard service full-time or part-time?
faqs.a: National Guard service is normally part-time: members typically train one weekend a month plus two weeks a year, while holding civilian jobs or attending college. However, members can be mobilized for state emergencies such as natural disasters, or federal missions including overseas deployments, during which service becomes full-time.

faqs.q: What benefits do National Guard members receive?
faqs.a: Members earn military pay and allowances, education benefits such as the GI Bill and tuition assistance, access to TRICARE Reserve Select health coverage, VA home loan eligibility, and retirement points toward a military pension. Many states also offer additional tuition waivers at public colleges for Guard members in good standing.

faqs.q: What is the service obligation for the National Guard?
faqs.a: Most enlistment contracts carry an eight-year service obligation, typically split between active drilling status and the Individual Ready Reserve. After initial training, members drill with their local unit while pursuing civilian careers. Officers commission through OCS, ROTC, or a service academy and serve under similar obligation terms.
